**Finding: LD — Compliant (preferred position).**

I reviewed every payment and termination mechanic that could operate as a Customer-payable stipulated sum:

- **Termination (Art. 12):** AbbVie may terminate for any or no reason on 90 days' notice (§12.3), and the consequences in §12.6.1 are limited to cessation of licences, reversion of Licensed Compounds/Products and data transfer — **no exit fee, minimum fee, or stipulated payment**. §12.7 reversion obligations run the other way (Harpoon pays royalties on the AbbVie Reversion IP licence). §12.9 simply preserves ordinary law/equity remedies with no stipulated sum.
- **Payments (Art. 6):** the $30M upfront and the milestone/royalty payments are ordinary consideration, not penalties; late-payment interest (§6.10) and audit cost-shifting on a material variance (§6.11) are customary mechanics.
- **Searches** for "liquidated damages", "penalty", "termination fee", "forfeit/stipulated/pre-estimate" and "minimum royalty" returned nothing operative against AbbVie; the only "penalties" reference is inside the mutual third-party indemnity (§11), which is not a Customer-payable LD.

No redline proposed — the absence of any Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalty satisfies the preferred element outright.
